items.summary: On some ROCm builds the C library rand() stream is reseeded by the runtime itself: on the first kernel launch the HIP runtime (CLR) compiles its internal copy (blit) kernels through comgr, and each comgr action creates a temp directory via LLVM sys::fs::createUniqueDirectory -> createUniquePath -> sys::Process::GetRandomNumber, which calls srand(<random seed>) once and then rand() (38 calls seen) when LLVM was built without arc4random (glibc < 2.36 at LLVM build time). TheRock's SDK on the fleet hosts (libLLVM.so.24.0git, GLIBC_2.27 symbols, imports srand/rand, no arc4random) does this; Ubuntu 24.04's libamd-comgr2 (distro LLVM 17, glibc 2.39) imports arc4random and does not. Not GPUMD's code objects loading: rand() after hipMalloc is still the default stream. GPUMD calls srand (or, under DEBUG, relies on the implicit seed 1) in print_compile_information() before the first HIP call, so the reseed overrides it; DEBUG builds that rely on the default stream (velocity without seed, add_random_force, curand seeds in lan/bao/pimd/ti...) then differ run to run, while velocity with an explicit seed (srand after GPU init) is unaffected and release builds only swap one random seed for another. Effect: tests_regression cases replicate_velocity_unseeded, graphene_hac, graphene_nemd_shc, graphene_hnemd_shc, silicon_liquid_transport and 4 tests_pytest spin force-modifier tests fail self-comparison on gfx942/gfx1100; all pass with an LD_PRELOAD shim that makes srand a no-op. Options: a HIP-only fix in GPUMD (e.g. seed after the first launch, or a private PRNG for DEBUG seeds), the ROCm report in comgr-llvm-srand-perturbs-host-rand, or accept as an AMD test-environment difference.

LLVM sys::Process::GetRandomNumber falls back to srand(GetRandomNumberSeed()) once plus rand() when the LLVM build lacks arc4random (glibc < 2.36 at build time, e.g. a manylinux glibc 2.28 build). comgr reaches it through createUniqueDirectory/createUniquePath for its temp directories (/tmp/comgr-<pid>-<n>-<hex>), and the HIP runtime (CLR) triggers that on the first kernel launch when it compiles its internal blit kernels from OpenCL C (COMPILE_SOURCE_WITH_DEVICE_LIBS_TO_BC, LINK_BC_TO_BC, CODEGEN_BC_TO_RELOCATABLE, LINK_RELOCATABLE_TO_EXECUTABLE). This reseeds the process-global C PRNG of any host program that seeds rand() for reproducibility. Seen with TheRock HIP 7.16.26385 (libLLVM.so.24.0git imports srand/rand, no arc4random) on gfx942 and gfx1100; backtrace hipLaunchKernel -> libamdhip64 -> amd_comgr_do_action -> GetRandomNumber -> srand. AMD_COMGR_USE_VFS and AMD_COMGR_CACHE do not avoid it. Not seen with Ubuntu 24.04's libamd-comgr2 (imports arc4random); the /opt/rocm packages are unchecked. Check: nm -D --undefined-only libLLVM*.so* libamd_comgr.so* | grep -w -e srand -e arc4random. Candidate report for a person to file, to comgr/TheRock (build LLVM so that arc4random or getrandom is used) or to LLVM (a library should not reseed the process-global C PRNG).
